Generating a chain of thought improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning.
nodes.evidence: Experiments on three large language models show that chain of thought prompting improves performance on a range of arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks.

nodes.label: Chain of thought reasoning abilities emerge naturally in sufficiently large language models via chain of thought prompting.
nodes.evidence: In particular, we show how such reasoning abilities emerge naturally in sufficiently large language models via a simple method called chain of thought prompting, where a few chain of thought demonstrations are provided as exemplars in prompting.

nodes.label: Prompting a 540B-parameter language model with just eight chain of thought exemplars achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on the GSM8K benchmark of math word problems.
nodes.evidence: For instance, prompting a 540B-parameter language model with just eight chain of thought exemplars achieves state of the art accuracy on the GSM8K benchmark of math word problems, surpassing even finetuned GPT-3 with a verifier.

nodes.label: Chain of Thought Prompting
nodes.description: A method where a few chain of thought demonstrations are provided as exemplars in prompting to improve complex reasoning in large language models.

nodes.label: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can be more effective when the target distribution is designed to account for token uncertainty and model prior.
nodes.evidence: TARGET-SFT, which constructs the training objective directly from the desired target distribution, consistently outperforms across the ten reasoning dataset-model settings evaluated.

nodes.label: The Q-target framework unifies many existing SFT variants by decomposing objective design into two explicit choices: how much to rely on the observed token and how to allocate the remaining probability mass.
nodes.evidence: The Q-target framework reveals that many existing SFT variants can be understood as varying ways of answering these two questions, and seemingly different losses correspond to implicit choices of target distribution Q.

nodes.label: TARGET-SFT adaptively balances strict imitation and prior preservation, leading to better performance on reasoning tasks.
nodes.evidence: TARGET-SFT consistently gives the best results across all models on both mathematical and medical reasoning tasks.

nodes.label: Q-target framework
nodes.description: A framework for supervised fine-tuning that decomposes the target distribution into two choices: how much to rely on the observed token and how to allocate the remaining probability mass.

nodes.label: UBP2 uses ensembles of reward, dynamics, and value function models to evaluate candidate trajectories according to a unified score.
nodes.evidence: Our method, Uncertainty-Balanced Preference Planning (UBP2), uses ensembles of reward, dynamics, and value function models to evaluate candidate trajectories according to a unified score that combines expected reward, terminal value, and epistemic uncertainty.

nodes.label: UBP2 establishes sublinear regret guarantees for both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon settings under standard regularity assumptions.
nodes.evidence: Under standard regularity assumptions, we establish sublinear regret guarantees for both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon settings.

nodes.label: The Reference Shortcut is a critical obstacle in conditioning a text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model on multiple reference voices and a free-form natural language prompt.
nodes.evidence: However, we identify a critical obstacle to this approach: the Reference Shortcut. During training under standard noise schedules, the model can identify the matching reference by acoustic similarity to the noisy target, bypassing the text prompt entirely.

nodes.label: A high-noise-biased timestep distribution addresses the Reference Shortcut by forcing the model to rely on the text prompt for speaker assignment.
nodes.evidence: We address this with a high-noise-biased timestep distribution that forces the model to rely on the text prompt for speaker assignment.

nodes.label: Mapping the information flow between denoising steps through an interpretable token bottleneck does not decrease downstream performance.
nodes.evidence: we show that we can map the information flowing between denoising steps through an interpretable token bottleneck with no decrease in downstream performance.

nodes.label: Reducing the opaque serial depth of DiffusionGemma to 1.1X that of Gemma 4 improves variable transparency.
nodes.evidence: Treating these intermediate states as interpretable reduces the opaque serial depth to just 1.1X that of Gemma 4.

nodes.label: Algorithmic transparency is more challenging for diffusion models compared to autoregressive models.
nodes.evidence: Algorithmic transparency is harder for diffusion models than for autoregressive models because all token predictions in the canvas can change at every denoising step, giving the model the power to implement complicated distributed algorithms during the denoising process.

nodes.label: DiffusionGemma exhibits novel diffusion-specific phenomena such as non-chronological reasoning, token and sequence smearing, and intermediate-context reasoning.
nodes.evidence: we conduct a suite of interpretability case studies, uncovering initial evidence of novel diffusion-specific phenomena such as non-chronological reasoning, token and sequence smearing, and intermediate-context reasoning.
